Analysis design

  • Diagnostic-model basis. The Diagnostic model fixes steepness at h = 0.90 and direct negative-binomial tag overdispersion at τ = 2, uses 33 independent selectivity groups with weak non-decreasing penalties for F10 and F33, and retains the Diagnostic-model DM settings.
  • One-at-a-time comparison. Each completed fit changes only its named sensitivity component. Model data, selectivity and other controls remain at their Diagnostic-model values unless they define the selected axis.
  • Lower τ sensitivity. Under the direct parameterization τ = 1 + exp(x), exactly τ = 1 would require x = log(0) = −∞ and cannot be represented by a finite parameter. The finite lower bound x = −5 therefore gives the near-one case τ = 1 + exp(−5) ≈ 1.00674.
  • Initialization. Every sensitivity is fitted independently from an ordinary makepar-generated initial PAR. It does not start from the fitted final PAR of the Diagnostic model, a selected jitter seed, or any fitted checkpoint.
  • Quantities. Figures compare annual dynamic spawning depletion, recruitment, spawning potential and fishing mortality. They are deterministic model comparisons and do not represent confidence intervals.
